Circular path antenna miniaturization and bandwidth improvement techniques are exploited for obtaining the optimum antenna which has a volume of 32.4 mm<sup>3</sup> (10 mm $\times 10$ mm $\times 0.324$ mm). A homogeneous muscle tissue is considered as a human body phantom for the design and Roger RT 5880 is used as the substrate material for the antenna. The antenna operates in two bands: lower band from 3.13 GHz to 3.6 GHz, and upper band from 5.87 GHz to 10.512 GHz. Results illustrate lower directivity of the antenna in both E-plane and H-plane. Maximum input power of 178 mW can be applied to the proposed antenna for limiting SAR value under the specific value (2W/kg) mentioned in IEEE C95.1-1999 safety standards.

articleTitle: Structural, optical and electrical properties of La - Mg co-substituted Bi0.5 Na0.5 TiO3 dielectric
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Lead free La-Mg co-substituted Bismuth Sodium Titanate (Bi<inf>0.5</inf> Na<inf>0.5</inf> TiO<inf>3</inf>; BNT) dielectric ceramic was synthesized by conventional solid-state reaction (SSR) route. The effects of La-Mg on the microstructural, optical, and electrical properties of BNT were systematically studied. The microstructure of Bi<inf>0.47</inf> La<inf>0.03</inf> Na<inf>0.50</inf> Ti<inf>0.97</inf> Mg<inf>0.03</inf> O<inf>3</inf> showed irregular shape surface grains with an average size of 2.37 ± 0.8 μm. The X-ray diffraction analysis of the co-substituted BNT revealed the formation of single phase rhombohedral R3c structure. An approximately 10% reduction in direct band gap to ~2.9 eV after La–Mg co-incorporation makes this compound a promising candidate for optoelectronic applications as compared to BNT (~3.2 eV). The frequency dependent complex impedance spectroscopic measurement revealed a moderate enhancement in dielectric constant along with a reduction in dielectric loss of BNT after the co-substitution. The frequency and temperature dependent variations in permittivity and loss tangent were explicated in terms of various types of polarization relaxation.

articleTitle: An ultra-low energy efficient topological field-effect transistor based on stanene under perpendicular electric field induced topological phase transition
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: To reduce energy dissipation in field-effect transistors on low-power applications such as switches, we have modeled a transistor made of 2D topological insulator zigzag stanene nanoribbon based on electric field-induced topological phase transition, which turns on and off the device. The transport properties and the device’s important parameters have been calculated by the tight-binding model and Non-Equilibrium Green’s Function formalism. The results show high on-state current density which can flow ballistically even in the presence of impurities and ultra-low dynamic power dissipation. Therefore, proof of the concept of the energy-efficient topological transistor is presented.

articleTitle: A New Topology of Single-Phase Transformerless Inverter for Reducing Leakage Current of Grid-tied Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: This paper is about a novel transformer-less grid connected single-phase photovoltaic inverter. Now-a-days fossil fuels are in scarce. So, renewables are the only way to fulfill the increasing energy crisis. Solar energy, tide energy, wind energy are different sources of renewable energies. Among those, solar energy is most reliable, cost-free, simple processing and mostly available energy source. The inverter topology described in this paper converts the dc power captured in photovoltaic cells to ac power and supplies it directly to the grid. The grid voltage and current THDs are kept below 2%; extensive leakage current flow has been controlled; and power quality is much improved by this unique inverter topology. The power switches have been controlled using SPWM in addition to unipolar control. However, the common mode voltage has remained constant, which has also helped to lower the leakage current to 7.205mA. In this topology with an LCL filter, eight super junction IGBTs and six diodes have been employed. With the help of simulation findings, the leakage current suppression has been thoroughly examined. The switches decreased the leakage current but had little impact on efficiency. This topology has been verified through MATLAB/Simulink software environment.

articleTitle: Cardio Vascular Disease prediction using machine learning with improved feature selection
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Due to the high susceptibility of Cardio Vascular Disease (CVD), a large percentage of people now run the risk of developing them. It has grown increasingly difficult day by day for clinical systems to anticipate CVDs early to avert severe health harm as the amount of afflicted persons is increasing. There is a demand for a system that operates with high precision at minimal computational cost in economically fragile nations. In this study, we used a hybrid model for feature selection with a neural learning approach to forecast CVD. Other classification algorithms are ANN, XGBoost, Random Forest, Multi Layer Perceptron, etc where ANN showed 75% accuracy similar to Random Forest after using feature selection algorithm. We discovered that the Decision Tree Classifier worked better than many machine learning techniques while ensembled with hardvoting and ANN.

articleTitle: An Efficient Triple-Error Correction Method for Memristor-Based Memory Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Memristor-based memory is an emerging technology that may replace conventional memories due to their compact size, higher density, lower power consumption, and non-volatile properties. Moreover, soft error immunity is considered one of the key factors which prefer one memory device over another. Therefore, a well-organized and effective soft error-correcting method is required to enhance the reliability of memristor-based memory. There is still negligible research on soft error tolerance in this field. Hence, this paper introduces a new error-correcting technique to tolerate soft errors in memristor-based memories. It can detect and correct up to three-bit soft errors in any memristor-based memory. Concerning existing techniques, the proposed method has lower information redundancy for the correction of all possible single, double, and triple-bit errors.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Network Based Feature Hybridization For Ct Scan Images: Covid-19 Detection Perspective
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Coronavirus disease (COVID-19) is an infectious disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus. Early diagnosis is only the proactive process to resist against the unwanted death. However, machine vision-based diagnosis systems show unparalleled success with higher accuracy and low false diagnosis rate. Working with the proposed method, this research has found that Computed Tomography (CT) provides more satisfactory outcomes regarding all the performance metrics. The proposed method uses a feature hybridization technique of concatenating the textural features with neural features. The literature review suggests that medical experts recommended chest CT in covid diagnosis rather than chest X- ray as well as RT-PCR. It is found that chest CT is more effective in diagnosis for being low false-negative rate. Moreover, the proposed method has used segmentation technique to dig the potential region of interest and obtain accurate features. Compared with different CNN classifier, such as, VGG-16, AlexNet, VGG-19 or ResNet50 and scratch model also. To obtain the satisfactory performance VGG-19 was used in this study. The Proposed machine learning based fusion technique achieves superior performance according to COVID-19 positive or negative with the accuracy of 98.63%, specificity of 99.08% and sensitivity of 98.18%.

articleTitle: Predicting Bum Injury Intensity from Skin Bum Images with Hybrid Machine Learning Technique
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Burns are one of the principal contributors of major clinical catastrophe, which can result in strong physiological reaction with long-lasting effects if patients are not appropriately treated. Predicting burn wound intensity at a preliminary phase is quite difficult, which is essential for proper burn treatment. Thus, a hybrid machine learning based approach has been proposed in this study to predict the bum injuiy intensity autonomously from skin bum images of patients. The proposed technique includes a Convolutional Neural Network(CNN) incorporating transfer learning method as the feature extractor from the input images and then conventional machine learning classification models as the classifiers for categorizing the images into three classes according to their bum severity: first, second and third degree bums. Ten different types of classification models have been trained and tested to explore the best performing one. Moreover, to validate the efficacy and potency of the proposed technique, the predictive analysis has also been carried out in another approach where digital image processing stages have been used as the feature extractor and then machine learning classification models as classifiers. According to the comparative evaluation findings, each classifiers using the suggested CNN architecture as feature extractor achieves noticeably higher accuracy and among them ‘XGBoost’ classification model outperforms others with 96.42% accuracy employing the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Voltage Stability Assessment of a Dual Active Bridge Based Solid State Transformer in a Smart Distribution System with Buck-Boost Converter
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Solid-state Transformer (SST) is a collection of high power semiconductor components and a high-frequency transformer, which enhances power quality by the means of preventing voltage imbalance and providing voltage regulation, harmonic filtering, reactive power compensation, disturbance & fault isolation. Due to its stronger electric field, quick switching capabilities, and extremely low switching loss, Silicon Carbide (SiC)-based Dual Active Bridge (DAB) is employed in the design of the SST. This topology has a buck-boost converter to regulate the output voltage for a variable input voltage. Buck-boost converter keeps the output voltage constant for any kind of voltage variation on the input side. This paper analyzes the functionality of the buck-boost converter to keep the voltage constant up to a 50% change in the input value to the desired output voltage. The future smart distribution system must have this controlled mechanism. Results from simulations using MATLAB are provided to illustrate the approach.

articleTitle: DenseLinkNet: A Deep Convolutional Architecture for Automatic Segmentation of Corneal Endothelial Cell
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Corneal endothelium cell provides vital clinical information regarding the health status of the cornea, which is crucial to monitor different corneal diseases. In this regard, segmentation of the corneal endothelial cell plays a significant role in assessing different clinical parameters, like cell density, coefficient of variation, and hexagonality, that aids clinicians in diagnosing different diseases. Since the manual observation process is both time-consuming and susceptible to errors, finding an efficient approach to automate the segmentation task is imperative. In this paper, an encoder-decoder based deep neural architecture, namely DenseLinkNet, is introduced to automate the segmentation process. In the proposed segmentation architecture, DenseNet-201 is used as an encoder, and LinkNet is used as a decoder. The encoder block exploits the output of the convolutional and dense blocks, and the generated feature map gets added with the corresponding decoder block. Following the process, a segmentation head is introduced to conclude the segmentation task. In this work, the publicly available Alizarine dataset is used for experimental purpose. The proposed DenseLinkNet architecture outperforms other segmentation networks with respect to different performance metrics. The network has achieved a dice-score of 76.82% and a Jaccard-index of 62.51%.

articleTitle: First-Principles Study on the Structural, Electronic and Optical Properties of Janus SiSSe Monolayer
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Janus two-dimensional materials have garnered research interest in recent times due to their intriguing properties arising from out-of-plane symmetry breaking. In this work, Janus monolayer SiSSe has been theoretically predicted and characterized by first-principles numerical calculations. The material is dynamically stable as there is no negative frequency in the phonon dispersion curves. The material is found to be mechanically stable on the basis of Born’s criteria. The electronic bandstructure reveals that the material possesses an indirect bandgap of 0.6501 eV. The bandgap can be tuned from 0.1003 eV to 0.9852 eV by the application of compressive and tensile biaxial strain. Moreover, at biaxial strain of −8%, the material undergoes a transition from semiconductor to metal. The optical properties of monolayer SiSSe are also investigated in this study. The absorption co-efficient has its major values within the UV region of the electromagnetic spectrum. The obtained results help to conclude that SiSSe is a promising candidate for switching applications and for devices that operate in the UV region.

articleTitle: X-ray Computed Tomography Sinogram Data Generation from Microwave Tomography Measurements Using Deep Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: X-ray computed tomography (CT) has been a widespread medical imaging modality for decades mainly due to its high imaging resolution. Compared to X-ray CT, microwave imaging (MWI) has several advantages, such as avoiding ionizing radiation, offering lower-cost portable hardware, etc. However, MWI lacks in terms of spatial resolution and robustness. In this work, we aim to bridge this gap by exploiting the strengths of MWI measurements and X-ray CT spatial resolution and combine them using a deep neural network (DNN). To our knowledge, for the first time, the trade-off between these two modalities is being addressed simultaneously. Using a customized Shepp-Logan phantom to emulate a simplified healthy human brain, we generated MWI data employing realistic dielectric properties of the head. Concurrently, the corresponding parallel beam X-ray CT data was generated. Next, a DNN comprised of several sub-networks was trained to successfully estimate the CT sinograms directly from the MWI measurements. Finally, the efficacy of the proposed method has been demonstrated through the successful estimation of CT sinograms (and subsequent image reconstructions) from MWI measurements for several thousand imaging scenarios.

articleTitle: Design of a Microstrip Antenna Having 360° Beam Steering Capability in Azimuth Plane
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: This paper proposes a beam steering microstrip antenna which can rotate the beam by 360° in azimuth plane. A circular microstrip patch is used as main radiating element with omnidirectional radiation and 24 rectangular strips which are responsible for 360° beam steering with non-uniform angular resolution of 10°-23° are connected rotationally around the circular radiating element by PIN diodes. When a PIN diode is turned ON selectively, then the main beam becomes directive according to the direction of the strip. Moreover, multiple diodes can be switched ON simultaneously to control the beamwidth of the radiation pattern. Omnidirectional radiation at3.79 GHz can be achieved by keeping all diodes OFF. The 10dB impedance bandwidth is 3.58 to 4.02 GHz for omnidirectional mode and 3.21 to 3.54 GHz for directional mode. The gain is 0.52 dBi for omnidirectional operation and 1.79 dBi for directional operation.

articleTitle: A Low-cost IoT-based Health Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: For early diagnosis of diseases, vital signs must be regularly checked. However, owing to the high cost, inadequacy, and complexity of monitoring devices, it is difficult for people to keep track of their vital signs at home. As a result, for health monitoring, a cost-effective, widely accessible, and simple-to-use system is required. In this study, the ESP32 micro-controller is used to create such a low-cost (approximately ${\$}$ 15), portable Internet-of-Things (IoT) based health monitoring system to make remote continuous monitoring and diagnostics feasible. Because of the low price, small size, and integrated Wi-Fi and Bluetooth module, the ESP32 is one of the greatest contenders for IoT-based health monitoring systems so far. In the proposed monitoring system, the lightweight Message Queue Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol was utilized. The data obtained through the system can be visualized in near real-time in a Graphical User Interface and also can be stored in a database for further analysis. The developed system has been tested and compared with medically certified equipment to validate the efficacy of the system.

articleTitle: An Improved Direct Torque Control Scheme for PWM Inverter Based Solar PV Array Fed Induction Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In this work, a space vector modulation (SVM) based direct torque control (DTC) of induction motor has been proposed to overcome the shortcomings of conventional DTC. One of the key features of SVM-based DTC is to reduce the torque ripple and provide a constant switching frequency. The proposed controller has a double-stage PI controller, which provides the necessary reference torque for the flux and torque controller loop. The two zero voltage vectors are deployed, which provides balanced and symmetric gate pulses to the VSI for efficient switching. Further, the IMD is supplied power from a solar PV array with maximum power point tracking (MPPT) facility. After that, a two-level pulse width modulated (PWM) voltage source inverter (VSI) is feeding power to the induction motor. All the simulation works are carried out in MATLAB/Simulink platform.

articleTitle: Enhancing average visible transmittance of CdS buffer layer for CuInGaSe based semi-transparent photovoltaics: metal ion substitution approach
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Integrating Semi-Transparent Photovoltaics (STPV) in buildings is the state-of-the-art application of thin-film photovoltaic (PV) technology, where $CuI{\mathrm{n}}_{1-\mathrm{x}}G\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{x}}Se2$ (CIGS) STPV cell shows promising outcomes. One possible reason for the reduced visible transparency of STPV devices is the undesired partial absorption of the visible spectrum by the cadmium sulfide (CdS) buffer layer. Further reducing this layer’s thickness to increase the average visible transmittance (AVT) will cause shunt losses, affecting the cell performance. This paper assesses the prospect of incorporating Zn in CdS to enhance the AVT of the buffer layer. A significant increase (24%) in AVT is observed in Zn-incorporated CdS film. The improved structural and optical properties and pin-hole-free, uniform morphology suggest that the substituted film is suitable as a buffer layer for CIGS-based STPV devices.

articleTitle: Application of Thermal Waste-to-Energy in Dhaka City: Benefits, Scope, and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Globally, municipal solid waste (MSW) accounts for around 4.5 million tons every day and it is anticipated that this amount will increase to more than 8 million tons per day by 2050. MSW accounts for more than 3.3% of global greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, and MSW management is widely acknowledged as a vital component of the government’s efforts to achieve sustainable development objectives. Modern waste-to-energy (WTE) facilities may avoid the production of methane (CH<inf>4</inf>), a member of GHG 25 times more potent than carbon dioxide (CO<inf>2</inf>) and other landfill emissions, and it is estimated that WTE saves between 0.5 and 1 ton of CO<inf>2</inf> equivalent GHG emissions per ton of waste when compared to landfills. Dhaka, one of the world’s most populous mega-cities, now dumps nearly all of its collected MSW in open landfills. According to the findings of this research, shifting one-quarter of pre-treated waste to WTE plants instead of landfills may cut up to one-third of CO<inf>2</inf> equivalent GHG emissions from landfills in Dhaka city annually. However, to make the WTE technology financially viable in Dhaka city, current legislative framework and public policies governing waste management system and energy sources need to be revised.

articleTitle: A Novel Non-Invasive Method to Measure Glucose Concentration Using Triple Pole CSRR Based Sensor
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: This paper presents a microwave biosensor for measurement of glucose concentration in aqueous glucose solution. The sensor comprises triple pole complementary split ring resonator (TP-CSRR). CSRRs of square and circular shape were designed and their performances were compared. A plexiglass container was put on the biosensor and glucose concentrations ranging 60 mg/dL to 300 mg/dL were applied on it. Permittivity of the glucose sample is changed by interacting with the highly concentrated electric field of the sensor. Amplitude of reflection coefficient of the sensor changes with the change in permittivity of the glucose sample. Glucose concentrations were measured from the change in reflection coefficient. The sensor with square and circular shaped CSRR has sensitivity of 1.16 dB per mg/dL and 4.37 dB per mg/dL respectively. This highly sensitive glucose sensor can measure glucose concentration with good accuracy.

articleTitle: An Analysis on Semidefinite Relaxation of Classical Optimal Power Flow Problem
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: A significant number of optimal power flow problems with positive semidefinite convex matrix and quadratic cost function can be resolved in polynomial time algorithm. In this paper we have considered the traditional optimal power flow problem considering line loss with bus injection model and reviewed the mathematical interpretations that allow to convert the problem in semidefinite programming. Any semidefinite programming can be solved efficiently with interior point method. We have summarized on previous results that the requirement for exactness to recover original solution depends on network structure. Finally we have verified our result with a IEEE benchmark system.

articleTitle: Benchmarking of Probabilistic-bit based Algorithm for Max-cut Problem
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In the age of big-data and internet of things combinatorial optimization problems (COP) have found widespread applications in both research and industry. However, solving these problems efficiently using deterministic approaches on conventional computers becomes challenging as the problem size and complexity increases. Recently, the concept of probabilistic computing utilizing probabilistic bits has gained attraction as an energy-efficient hardware accelerator for randomized algorithms. In this paper, we explore simulated annealing using probabilistic bits in solving the most popular COP - max-cut problem. The performance of the algorithm is benchmarked against 50 G-set connection graphs, where the best cut was found for 11 graphs and the deviations for the others were minimal.

articleTitle: Levelized Cost of Energy and Cost-Benefit Analysis of 230 kV Bulk Power Transmission in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: We examine the fiscal components of power transmission schemes in this paper, focusing on the feasibility of developing 230 kV transmission infrastructure to provide an area with high-quality, dependable energy source. Bulk power from generating stations with a combined installed capacity of over 250-300 MW is usually evacuated at 230 kV for long distance transmission in Bangladesh. With the growing number of large scale conventional and renewable power plants penetrating the grid, the Transmission System Operator now must expand the evacuation facilities, guarantee reliability, and preserve contingency. The paper determines the threshold scope, time, and cost of 230 kV power transmission in Bangladesh. Three types of substations and four different types of lines have been examined. The combinations result in twelve different technical configurations that are studied in this paper. To assure the credibility of the investment, we employ the Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) method. The model is customized to yield the threshold evacuation span. A computer aided power flow solution optimizes the model inputs for a valid return. Using this threshold, payback time is derived as a forecasting tool to choose among alternatives. Finally, in response to anticipated integration of conventional/ renewable sources to the grid, levelized cost of energy transmission is calculated for multiple climatic geolocations combining the fixed costs and variable costs into a single measurement.

articleTitle: Design of a Hexad-Polarization Antenna With High Isolation and Switchable Feed Network
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: This article presents a multi-layer hexad-polarization compatible reconfigurable square shaped patch antenna. With an intent to use in the sub–6 GHz spectrum, the proposed antenna’s polarization can be switched among horizontal linear polarization (LP), vertical LP, slant ±45° LP, right-hand circular polarization (RHCP), and left-hand CP (LHCP) by controlling PIN diodes in switchable feed network. By incorporating two orthogonal aperture-coupled switchable feed networks and a 180° phase shifter, the proposed antenna can operate at single or dual feeding mode. The horizontal and vertical LP can be attained by exciting single port. On the other hand, slant +45° LP, –45° LP, RHCP, and LHCP can be achieved by switchable dual port excitation. Low cross-polarization and high isolation in each mode make the proposed antenna more attractive for wireless applications. The proposed antenna has 10-dB impedance bandwidth of 1.19% for LP, 0.89% for LHCP, and 1.19% for RHCP. Moreover, 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 5.97% for RHCP and 7.19% for LHCP are attained. Better isolation characteristic (<-25 dB) is achieved at resonance frequency of 3.34 GHz without utilizing any isolation improvement techniques. The maximum gains of two CP modes and the LP mode are 6.8 dBic, 6.2 dBic, and 6.45 dBi, respectively.

articleTitle: Assessment of Polyurethane Nanofiber with Nikel as Terahertz Metamaterial and Strain Sensor
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: This study aims to develop mechanical tunable metamaterials operating at wideband terahertz frequencies (up to 30 THz) for mapping strain in opaque composite materials. This study has produced thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) nanofiber matrix with nickel nanoparticle (TPU-Ni) using electrospun nanofiber technology. We have characterized the morphological, electrochemical, and mechanical properties of produced TPU-Ni composite. We also measured the response of the T-ray wave of TPU-Ni as a function of strain by applying a stretching force to the composite using a T-ray time-domain spectroscopy. Scanning electron microscopy image with EDS analysis confirms the embedding of Ni nanoparticles with the polymer matrix. Cyclic voltammetry tests on TPU-Ni nanofiber measured a current peak for the applied voltage. Pull-out tension tests found that the TPUNi polymer matrix is flexible and has sufficient strength to be used as a sensing material for highly sensitive strain gauge applications. THz reflected intensity as a function of a strain of TPU-Ni for five repeated reversal loading cycles shows fully recoverable strain in repeated load cycles. This study concluded that the TPU-Ni composite has the potential to be used for flexible terahertz metamaterial-based sensor applications.

articleTitle: Development of a Low-Cost Prototype of Blood Warmer and Rapid Infuser
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Rapid blood infusion is a life-saving technology during an emergency or a surgical intervention. Since blood banks preserve whole blood by refrigerating at $(1-6)^{\circ}C$, to avoid hypothermic shock, it is suggested to infuse the blood into the body at a temperature of $37^{\circ}C$, the homeostatic core temperature of the human body. However, existing solutions are expensive for a hospital with average financial resources. This calls for developing a low-cost device capable of highspeed delivery of warmed blood. In this work, a fully-functional prototype of such a device has been developed using a peristaltic pump, a heating plate connected with a thermostat, a 3D printed heating mold, and a calibration-based voltage control mechanism. The heating mechanism is adequately regulated and ensured to be contamination free. The flow rate is quantified via the calibration system concerning the applied voltage and temperature parameters. The prototype has demonstrated a flow rate in the range of 3-12 mL/min, and the heating rate is found to be approximately $0.75^{\circ}C/min$; these values closely resemble the parameters of the commercial set-ups. Moreover, the expenditure for the development of the current prototype is as low as $\sim 100$ USD making it financially more accessible than the commercially available units. Although the results highlight the potential of the developed prototype for the low-resource settings with adequate proof of concept, it is imperative to further optimize the design, functionality, and safety factors through proper bench-top testing protocols and in vivo experiments.

articleTitle: Priority Based Hybrid Renewable Energy Monitoring and Management System with SCADA Autonomous Operation Based on Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In this paper, a load management has been discussed which is maintained by five power sources including three main power sources – wind power, solar, biomass and two backup power sources – battery banks and diesel generator. A village consisting of 18 categories of load with different capacities enjoy this generated power for 24 hours based on source energy priority and load consumption. A SCADA autonomous system controls the power distribution throughout the village which ensures the proper utilization of the energy and increases the efficiency of power control. Furthermore, the consumer will be protected from blackout and will get uninterrupted power throughout the day and night based on priority settings.

articleTitle: Investigation of MoS₂/Perovskite/WSe₂ on Si Tandem Structure of Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Owing to high efficiency in terms of power (PCE), perovskite material based solar cells (PSCs) are receiving the most attention from the researchers. In this work, we will suggest a novel transport layer combination that significantly improves device performance. The capability of our device will be demonstrated using the SCAPS-ID simulator. In order to design a tandem solar cell, this novel Perovskite layer is ultimately be used to design the top cell and bottom one is proposed with crystalline silicon. We have investigated that using MoS<inf>2</inf> (ETL) and WSe2 (HTL) as charge transport layer incorporated with absorber layer, MAPbI3, accomplish our goals after simulating every available parameter carefully. We have achieved upto 25.03% power conversion efficiency, fill factor (FF) of 88.26%, short circuit current density ($\mathrm{J}_{\mathrm{s}\mathrm{c}}$) of 27.62 mA/cm<sup>2</sup>, and open-circuit voltage ($\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{c}}$) of 1.03V using this combination and their thickness modification. Considering defects in different layers the results are reduced to 22.63%, 85.34%, 26.S9mA/cm<sup>2</sup> and 0.99V respectively. At last, we have proposed a tandem solar cell consisting a crystalline silicon incorporated bottom cell to improve quantum efficiency (QE) and utilize more spectrum. With 0.76V$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{c}}$, 38.63mA/cm<sup>2</sup>$\mathrm{J}_{\mathrm{s}\mathrm{c}}$, and approximately 85.26% FF, the bottom Si cell has a PCE of 24.97%. The overall PCE of the tandem cell as a whole is 41.5 percent with $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{c}}$ of 1.74V, 87.12% FF, and 27.14SmA/cm<sup>2</sup> of $\mathrm{J}_{\mathrm{s}\mathrm{c}}$.

articleTitle: Performance Augmentation of an Arc Suppression Device using Particle Swarm Optimization Based Proportional Resonant Controller
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: This work proposes the control of an are suppression device (ASD) using the particle swarm optimization (PSO) based proportional-resonant controller. Neutral point voltage control has been performed to reach zero voltage at the faulty phase, thereby achieving sufficient suppression of the fault current so that the sustainment of the arc becomes impossible. Therefore, the probability of a powerline bushfire has significantly reduced. The advantage of voltage control-based regulation of ASD over current injection-based control is that the performance of ASD is independent of the fault resistance. At first proportional-integral (PI) controller was designed for the outer voltage and inner current control loop using the PSO algorithm. Then, the design is extended to the proportional-resonant (PR) controller for the voltage control loop and the PI controller for the current control loop. The PSO-PR voltage controller enabled a better tracking of the reference voltage and ensured reduced fault current than classical PI and PSO-PI-based design. The integral time absolute error (ITAE) cost function achieved using PSO-PR was 83.12% less than the classical PI controller and 36.32% less than the PSO-PI controller. The modeling and simulation of the system have been performed in MATLAB/Simulink platform.

articleTitle: Transport Layer Material and Thickness Optimization of Cs₂TiBr₆ Based Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Although perovskite solar cell is seeing tremendous success as a solar cell of third-generation, toxicity and stability are two significant obstacles that it needs to overcome yet. To triumph over these two challenges, an inorganic lead-free and nontoxic perovskite Cs<inf>2</inf> TiBr<inf>6</inf> has been presented to have impressive environmental stability and excellent photoelectric properties as a direct bandgap material, confirmed from various experiments recently. This work investigates the solar cell with FTO/ETL/Cs<inf>2</inf> TiBr<inf>6</inf>/HTL/Au structure and conducts simulation studies in the most crucial device physics aspects to improve the performance. By determining viable electron-hole transport layer, this study suggests an optimum thickness of 245 nm for the perovskite absorber layer in FTO/TiO<inf>2</inf>/Cs<inf>2</inf> TiBr<inf>6</inf>/MoO<inf>3</inf>/Au structure to possess a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 15.02%. And this optimum thickness of the absorber increases dramatically with diffusion length. The findings of this study provide insight into the much higher impact of defect densities and diffusion length than transport layers (HTL& ETL).

articleTitle: Efficient Self-Supervised Denoising from Single Image
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Despite being challenging, research on single image based denoising is enjoying a recent upsurge due to the impressive and dominating performance of deep networks. Most of the self supervised single image denoising methods need noisy training pair to learn the denoising function, which, however, often undergoes identity mapping and overfitting while training. A recent work, Self2Self, proposed a Bernoulli-dropout based denoising schema that removes random pixel information to escape identity mapping. Nonetheless, real camera noises are signal dependent, and typically poses trivial changes to the images. Hence, pixels on an area might still preserve similar contextual information even under such a pixel-dropout strategy, raising the chance of suffering identity mapping. In this work, we address this critical issue by generating the training pair by randomly masking out square regions rather than simple Bernoulli-dropping, which provides a better chance to evade the relevant contextual information. Training pair is passed to the network within a self supervised loss to generate single predicted image at each iteration, which are then averaged to acquire the final denoised image. We evaluate our method under the presence of additive and real world noise, and observe better performance against existing traditional and self-supervised based models.

articleTitle: A Naive Bayes Classifier Based Energy Scheduling for Home Energy Management System (HEMS)
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: With the increase of domestic energy consumption, an efficient energy management scheme for smart home is needed. Just as solar power can be used as a supplement to grid power in order to use smart appliances in case of grid unavailability or blackout. In this research, a load and power management system based on load priority and instant grid energy price has been proposed using Fuzzy logic algorithms. The home energy management systems (HEMS) modeled using Naive Bayes classifier shows that the loads can be shifted on or off based on grid availability, solar availability, pricing demand, urgency and loads can be changed their power source based on Interrupted, Non-interrupted, and Fixed appliances. This sort of technologies would be needed in Bangladesh whereas cost adopts grid energy price variation over time and demand. Simulation results reveal that the proposed protocol saves 47.1% ~ 48.47% of monthly electricity cost compare to the traditional scheme.

articleTitle: Comparison of Optoelectronic Characteristics of Carbon Thin Films Electrodeposited on Silicon and Zinc Substrates
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Carbon thin films were deposited on Silicon (Si) and Zinc (Zn) substrates by electrodeposition in methanol solution. The role of camphor (C10H16O) incorporation in methanol is studied. In the electrodeposition arrangement Si and Zn substrates were mounted individually on the negative electrodes in camphoric methanol solution. A variable dc voltage source is applied between the electrodes to get better current density in methanol solution during the electrodeposition process. The carbonic thin films deposited on Si and Zn substrates for different percentage of camphor were analyzed by Fourier Transform of Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopic scheme and measurement of optical absorption, transmittance and reflectance by UV-VIS-IR spectroscopic arrangement. Presence of hydrogenated amorphous carbon (a-C: H) bond were observed for the films deposited on Si substrates. The FTIR spectroscopy also indicates existence of both sp<sup>2</sup> and sp<sup>3</sup> C-H stretch for the films electrodeposited on Si substrate. But there is no clear evidence of the presence of hydrogenated amorphous carbon (a-C: H) bond or sp<sup>2</sup>/sp<sup>3</sup> C-H stretch for the film deposited on Zn substrate. So Si is more suitable for preparing semiconducting carbon thin films. In the UV-VIS-IR spectroscopy camphor can influence the absorption spectrum of the films deposited on both Si and Zn substrates. In both of the cases increase of camphor, increases the absorption of photon energy. So camphoric methanol solution can influence the optoelectronic properties of carbon thin films, electrodeposited on Si and Zn substrates.

articleTitle: Static Hand Gesture Recognition by RCDT Classifier
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: With technological advancement, automated hand gesture recognition has become an essential tool for a group of people who are deaf or mute, or both. In addition, the use of hand gestures provides an effective way of communication between humans and computers. In literature, most automatic hand gesture classification techniques are devised on neural network architecture. Although these techniques provide good classification accuracy, they often require the intensive use of additional GPU and larger training data sets. In this paper, we have proposed a heuristic approach to recognizing static hand gestures based on the Radon Cumulative Distribution Transform (RCDT) with a mean accuracy of 99.485%. This performance evaluation is conducted employing only 32 training samples with 10-fold cross-validation. The results can be reproduced by the MATLAB code available at https://github.com/KamrulHasan1743/rcdt_Classifier.

articleTitle: A Mathematical Modelling of Discharge and Charge Phenomena of A Lead-Acid Battery
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: A mathematical model has been formulated and verified with experimental data to describe a lead acid battery’s discharging and charging characteristics here. First, an overview of the empirical formula and the corresponding circuit model for discharging has been explained in this work. Then a set of 25 battery samples has been discharged at different C-rate to obtain discharge data (voltages vs SOC) to evaluate all the parameters in the model. Next, simulation has been performed with the model from the existing formula and the results have been compared with each of the battery samples. Finally, the parameters have been set from that particular battery for which the simulated value gives a minimum error with all the other battery discharge data from the set. Conclusively the discharge model with all of its parameters has been verified with battery sets of different capacities. For charging, the existing formula has been modified to represent the over-charging phenomenon at higher SOC. Then all of the parameters have been selected by analyzing all of the experimental data from a set of few battery samples. The final value of the parameters has been chosen for which the error is minimum. Battery temperature, average DOD, and battery lifetime are all of these variables that have been considered to be constant for the obtained experimental data here.

articleTitle: Analysis of Coupling Coefficient and Source Frequency Variations in Basic Compensation Topologies of MRC Based WPT Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Magnetic Resonance Coupling (MRC) based Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) system is gaining popularity due to its increased power transfer capacity. However, this method is very dependent on the alignment and resonant frequency of the transmitter and receiver coils. A little misalignment might cause the loss of the resonant point and a significant decrease in output power. This research examines the effect of misalignment of coils via coupling coefficient and the effect of operating frequency fluctuation on the output power of MRC-based WPT system for four fundamental compensation topologies. The investigation demonstrates that series-series (SS) topology is the most tolerant of misalignment of coils, whilst parallel-parallel (PP) topology is the most stable against operating frequency variation from resonant point. Parallel-series (PS) topology is the least tolerant to coil misalignment and operating frequency variations among all basic topologies.

articleTitle: Structural, electronic and optical characterization of edge passivated B and P doped GaN nanostructures
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In this work, using first principles within the framework of Density-functional theory, we have explored the structural, electronic, and optical properties of two-dimensional edge passivated pristine GaN nanostructures along the zigzag direction. The indirect bandgap of pristine GaN can be tuned by chemical doping and the impurity atom size and doping concentration have a significant impact on the stability of these doped structures. Under both Ga-rich and N-rich circumstances, the effects of boron and phosphorus impurity concentrations have been investigated. The complex dielectric function is significantly modulated for all the structures. There is a noticeable shift in peak position, and lowered peak strength in the spectrum. Due to the newly created impurity states in the forbidden region, additional inter-band transitions are also seen, leading to some discernible peaks in the lower energy range. Based on the influence of chemical doping, it is expected that boron and phosphorus doped GaN nanostructures are potentially suitable for optoelectronic, photocatalyst, visible, and UV detector applications.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis of COVID-19 Vaccination in Bangla Language with Code-Mixed Text from Social Media
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: The vaccination program which helps avert pandemics is facing new hurdles, including the emergence of hazardous new virus strains and public distrust. Analyzing the sentiment expressed in social media interactions related to vaccines may aid the health authority in implementing public safety procedures and guide the government in developing appropriate policies. The purpose of this research is to identify the public sentiments toward the COVID-19 vaccination in Bangladesh from social media comments. Comments posted on social media platforms often mix formal and informal language known as code-mixed text and do not adhere to any particular grammatical standards. In addition, the Bangla language lacks computational models and annotated resources for sentiment analysis. To overcome this, we created CoVaxBD, a Bangla-English code-mixed and sentiment-annotated corpus of Facebook comments. This paper also proposes a model for sentiment analysis based on the multilingual BERT. It achieves a validation accuracy of around 97.3 % and a precision score of approximately 97.4%.

articleTitle: Impact of System Parameters on EHV Line Shunt Reactor Requirements
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: For long transmission lines, synchronization becomes a challenge due to excessive capacitive MVAr produced by the line itself. This phenomenon is known as Ferranti effect. To reduce the Ferranti effect in EHV lines, line shunt reactors are typically applied at transmission lines ends. Optimum sized line shunt reactor helps reduce line losses and subsequently increases voltage profile and line loadability. Line length have major impact on reactor requirement ampersand its size. System strength in terms of high ampersand low short circuit level will have impact on system voltage profile during lightly ampersand heavily loaded conditions. This, in effect, will play a vital role in EHV Reactor Requirement. The system strength impact on the line shunt reactor requirements is investigated in this paper.

articleTitle: Modeling Second Order Anisotropy of Monodomain Magnetic Body
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: The switching of a ferromagnet’s magnetization direction is a fundamental aspect in modeling spintronic devices. The switching can be achieved by applying an external magnetic field or spin current, and one of the key determinants of the switching process is the magnetocrystalline anisotropy. To model the magnetization dynamics, considering only the first order magnetocrystalline perpendicular anisotropy contributions had been sufficient thus far as it’s contributions are predominant. However, as the dimensions of the magnetic body are scaled down, or subject to voltage control of anisotropy (VCMA) effect, the magnetocrystalline perpendicular anisotropy and the out-of-plane demagnetizing field both end up having equal order, and nowadays low barrier magnets are purposefully designed to have magnetic anisotropy close to zero for special applications. In these cases, the contribution of the second order anisotropy of the ferromagnet need to be considered while studying the magnetization dynamics. In this paper, we developed a physics-based SPICE-compatible compact model of a monodomain magnetic body considering the second-order magnetic anisotropy contributions. The magnetization dynamics are described by the stochastic Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (sLLG) equation and can be used to study both perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA) magnets and in-plane magnetic anisotropy (IMA) magnets. Here, we studied the effect of second order anisotropy in the critical switching field and current for PMA magnet and found that the second-order contributions to the switching field and current become significant when it is in the same order as the first order anisotropy.

articleTitle: Design of Circuit Parameters for Series-Parallel Compensation Topology in Critical Magnetic Resonance Coupling
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: The magnetic resonance coupling (MRC) technique is mostly utilized in the near field wireless power transfer (WPT) as power transfer can be maximized using this technique by ensuring critical coupling between transmitter and receiver coils. Among the existing basic compensation topologies of this technique, the Series-Parallel (SP) topology is studied in this paper. Although these basic topologies have been extensively studied, mathematical relationships between the resonant frequency and circuit parameters at critical coupling for all the topologies have not been established yet. In this study, a generalized equation for the resonant frequency at critical coupling condition for SP topology is proposed and simulation is conducted to verify the proposed equation. The observed results are in full compliance with the theoretical findings of the study.

articleTitle: A modified CNN model for diagnosing schizophrenia disease using fMRI data
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Schizophrenia is a debilitating and persistent mental disorder. It manifests as cognitive, emotional, and behavioral limitations with various degrees of social function impairment that get worse with time. To identify those limitations, a deep learning-based neuroimaging technique is feasible to detect. In the last two decades, neuroimaging, precisely functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) has become indispensable for investigating the brain image processing and related abnormalities of schizophrenia patients. We proposed a modified Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model based on VGG16. Along with our proposed model, a set of CNN models—VGG16, VGG19, EfficientNet, Inception V3, and ResNet-50 have been considered to identify schizophrenia and healthy controls. We evaluated correlation analysis on time series feature extractions over Open-NEURO clinical dataset and achieved accuracy of schizophrenia detection of 99.5%. Moreover, Receiver Operating characteristic Curve (ROC) have been generated to compare with existing reference models. This research significantly affects the primary detection of schizophrenia and might prevent a patient from mental disorder at an early stage.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-based Alcoholism Detection Using Higuchi’s Fractal Dimension Features from EEG
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Alcoholism is a well-known mental health problem that affects behavior and emotional functioning. Excessive drinking of alcohol affects a person’s personal and social life in addition to causing mental diseases such as hallucinations, agitation, memory loss, difficulty in making decisions, and issues focusing. According to studies, employing various machine learning algorithms, alcoholism can be detected from different brain signals, particularly electroencephalography (EEG). This study investigates the classification performance of Neural Network (NN) with Higuchi’s fractal dimension (HFD) features from selected EEG channel data using the XGBoost algorithm. The classification accuracy is 94.79% using all channels while using selected channels it is also 94.16%. The selected channel-based NN classification model appears optimistic with a reduced number of channels without a significant reduction in accuracy.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine Driven Energy Efficient Low Power Fuel Cell Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Hydrogen fuel cell vehicles are becoming very popular but most of them use high power electrical motors that quickly burn hydrogen fuel. To address this concern, a low power permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) driven energy efficient fuel cell electric vehicle (FCEV) is proposed in this paper. A proton exchange membrane hydrogen fuel cell (PEMFC) is used as an electricity generator to drive the PMSM. The fuel cell creates energy electrochemically where low dc voltage rating is obtained. A dc-dc boost converter is applied to increase the voltage rating. To drive the PMSM, an inverter is coupled to the boost converter to create suitable voltage and frequency. This paper analyzes the performance of the FCEV at different fuel flow rates. To get the best performance, an optimization is carried out, keeping the fuel flow rate at its optimum value. MATLAB-Simulink is used to analyze different segments of the FCEV. Various parameters of the fuel cell, converter, and the PMSM are plotted in the result section.

articleTitle: Effect of Quantum Repetition Code on Fidelity of Bell States in Bit Flip Channels
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Quantum Entanglement is a key to establish secure communication between two nodes in a communication channel. Ensuring high fidelity entanglement has always been a challenging task owing to interaction with the hostile channel environment. Several methods have been proposed in this paper to mitigate the problem. It has been shown that fidelity can be improved by encoding bell pairs using Quantum Repetition Codes (QRCs). In this regard, various QRC-based techniques are also analyzed mathematically, and their performances have been compared.

articleTitle: Development of Algorithm to Extract Features from Capnograph Signal
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Cardiopulmonary diseases are generally detected using spirometry and peak expiratory flow meter which is tedious for a patient for the fastest blow required. Hence doctors recommend using Capnography which detects the CO2 saturation level from exhaled breath. This paper gives an algorithm to detect vital features from the Capnographic datasets (available in capnobase) which might be suitable for classifying cardiopulmonary diseases like Asthma, COPD, hypoventilation, hyperventilation, etc. Some of the signals are composed of artifacts while some are of spontaneous breath which makes it difficult to identify and extract the features properly. We propose a method to extract a total of 25 features from the Capnograph automatically using digital signal processing. We also identified the significant differences for apnea and cardiogenic oscillation. Among the features, some of them are slopes that properly fit with the original signal with 99.95% sensitivity for regular Capnogram and about 97-99% for irregular Capnogram.

articleTitle: Start-End Writing Integration with Convolutional Neural Network for Bengali Handwritten Numeral Recognition
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Convolutional neural network (CNN) based methods have been very successful for handwritten numeral recognition (HNR) applications. However, CNN seems to misclassify similar shaped numerals (i.e., the silhouette of the numerals that look same). This paper presents an enhanced HNR system to improve the classification accuracy of the similar shaped handwritten numerals incorporating the terminals points (i.e., the start and end positions) with CNN’s recognition. Start-End Writing Measure (SEWM) and its integration with CNN is the main contribution of this research. Traditionally, CNN’s classification (i.e., $\mathrm{C}\mathrm{L}_{\mathrm{C}\mathrm{N}\mathrm{N}}\in\{0,1, \ldots,9\})$ for highest probability is the outcome of CNN-based system. In the proposed system, along with classification in CLCNN, its probability value (say CNN’s confidence level 0CNN) is also used as a regulating element. Parallel to CNN’s classification operation, SEWM measures start-end points of the numeral image, suggests CLSEWM numeral category for which measured start-end points are found closed to reference start-end points of the numeral class. Finally, output label or system’s classification $(\mathrm{C}\mathrm{L}\mathrm{s}_{\mathrm{y}\mathrm{s}})$ of the given numeral image is provided comparing 0CNN with predefined threshold value (o0): CNN’s outcome is considered as system’s outcome $(i.e., \mathrm{C}\mathrm{L}\mathrm{s}_{\mathrm{y}\mathrm{s}}=CLcNN)$ if $0CNN = \gt \sigma 0$; otherwise, SEWM rectifies CNN’s decision (i.e., $\mathrm{C}\mathrm{L}\mathrm{s}_{\mathrm{y}\mathrm{s}}=$CLsEWM) as CNN’s confidence is low. The proposed method is tested on rich benchmark numeral datasets of Bengali and revealed itself as a suitable HNR method.

articleTitle: RiIG Modeled Curvelet Coefficient Image-based Breast Tumor Classification Using deep CNN
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Deep learning-based automatic classification of breast tumors using ultrasound (US) B-Mode images is still a challenging research area. A deep convolutional neural network employing parametric imaging is presented to categorize benign and malignant breast tumors from ultrasound B-Mode images. The Rician Inverse Gaussian (RiIG) distribution is used to represent the statistics of breast US imaging data in the domain of the Curvelet Transform. In different Curvelet sub-bands, locally estimated values of the RiIG distribution’s dispersion parameters produce parametric images. A publicly accessible dataset of 780 breast ultrasound images along with their ground truth images is used for classification with a specially designed convolutional neural network. The proposed technique yields 97.1%, 96.6%, 97.3%, 94.3%, and 98.4% accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV), respectively, higher than those of several recently reported techniques.

articleTitle: Zero-Shot Entity Representation Learning for Temporal Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Temporal Knowledge Graphs (TKG) are multi-relational graphs where time is an important dimension. The research interest in TKG is increasing very rapidly. Despite recent advancements, there still exist some unexplored areas such as, Zero-Shot Learning (ZSL) which aim’s to identify the embeddings of unseen entities. To deal with zero-shot learning we use both structural and textual descriptions of entities. For structural representation, we incorporate time directly into the vector space. For textual representation, we collect text descriptions of entities and use Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to capture the semantic features of the text descriptions. We utilize both of the aforementioned representations in the same vector space. Thus, we can utilize both structural and semantic representations of an entity which helps us to analyze the context of the entity. To test our model we utilized YAGO and Wikidata, two commonly used temporal knowledge graphs. We compare our method with two baseline methods. The evaluation result shows that our proposed method outperforms other methods for identifying relationships of unseen entities with proper time annotations.

articleTitle: PV with Storage System for Demand Management
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Solar power is a good option in reducing grid electricity demand. Solar Photovoltaic (PV) panel with Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) is increasingly used to utilize solar energy for peak demand reduction and consumer’s peak shifting from on-peak hour to off-peak hour. This paper presents a sizing methodology of BESS to reduce peak demand at desired percentage. An algorithm has been developed to schedule the charging and discharging power of BESS with an aim to reduce daily operation cost based on peak demand charge reduction and time of use (ToU) energy price. Variation of real-time demand and solar PV output has been addressed with adaptive control measures. The proposed algorithm is applied to residential and non-residential consumers whose peak demand occurs at evening and mid-day respectively. The result shows a promising reduction in consumer’s daily operation cost.

articleTitle: Spectral-Spatial Feature Reduction for Hyperspectral Image Classification with Optimized Technique Series
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) is increasingly being used in a wide range of practical applications. High correlations between and within classes, the curse of dimensionality, and overfitting have all piqued the interest of researchers. Because of the excellent feature extraction and good overall performance, deep learning-based algorithms with dimensionality reduction methods have been recommended as a viable alternative for hyperspectral image analysis. Principal component analysis (PCA) and Sparse PCA (SPCA) are commonly used in dimensionality reduction. Because each principal component is a linear mixture of the original variables, principal component analysis (PCA) is difficult to interpret, and SPCA cannot choose the most relevant features. To overcome the issue, a mutual information-based greedy feature selection approach called minimum redundancy maximum relevancy (mRMR) is combined with SPCA (SPCA-mRMR). Many deep learning combination techniques rely on the 2D and 3D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) methodologies. A fused 3D-2D CNN model is less difficult than a 3D-CNN alone, yet it can also operate effectively in noisy settings with few training examples. Therefore, SPCA-mRMR and fused 3D-2D CNN are used to create a hybrid model called HMC-NET for HSI classification. Several optimization strategies are used to address overfitting and improve classification accuracy. To assess the efficacy of this proposed technique, performance results were compared to highly regarded models with fewer variables.

articleTitle: Motor Imagery Hand Movement Classification Using Attention Network Integrated Inception Model
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In the Brain Computer Interface (BCI) system, classification of hand movements using brain activity is a very significant task. The use of this classification in medical and biomedical applications has expanded, particularly for people with disabilities. In this context, time series data based on electroencephalogram (EEG) are utilized to capture brain signals and perform classification tasks. While several machine learning-based techniques can accurately classify intra-subject data validation, cross-subject validation remains inadequate. To this end, a novel method is proposed in this paper to classify hand movements (cross-subject) by incorporating an attention mechanism (squeeze-and-excitation) with a modified inception-V1 model. In order to filter out less significant channels and data, input data is first simultaneously passed through a squeeze-and-excitation block and a ID convolutional block. The squeeze-and-excitation block is further followed by two ID convolution sub-branches. Moreover, inception modules are utilized to extract local sparse features from the data. The proposed model is evaluated on the well-known BCI-2000 motor imaging dataset. The model demonstrates an accuracy of 84.75% in cross-subject validation, by doing so, the proposed approach substantially outperforms several state-of-the-art methods. In the context of BCI, this research work has the potential to be utilized as an effective resource for future hand movement classification-based applications.

articleTitle: A low cost Ni-based planar multilayer structure for passive heating of buildings
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In this work we examine the performance of a planar multilayer structure for passive heating of windows. Our analysis indicates that Ni is a promising material for such applications. We also find that control of thickness will be critical to ensure satisfactory optical and thermal performance is achieved.

articleTitle: Design of a Metamaterial Perfect Absorber: A Solar Energy Harvester
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: A contrived, as well as novel structure of metamaterial perfect absorber (MPA), is proposed based on vanadium dioxide (VO<inf>2</inf>). Vanadium dioxide undergoes an almost three times increase in electrical conductivity in the so-called terahertz gap. It has been numerically demonstrated that, this proposed synthesis of metal-insulator-metal exhibits a higher absorption rate of greater than 99% with a central frequency of 4.5 THz in the THz gap which seems more feasible than previous reports contingent on VO<inf>2</inf>. This novel structure has strong potential for solar energy harvesting, modulation, switching, sensors, imaging, and high-bit-rate communication in the terahertz gap range.

articleTitle: Design of a Highly Randomized Crossover Ring Oscillator Physical Unclonable Function
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Silicon Physical Unclonable Function (PUF) is the most critical hardware security circuit that exploits unique identification or random key generation utilizing manufacturing process variations. Numerous PUFs are in the literature amongst Ring Oscillator (RO) PUFs are mainly used for their simple structures. However, the uniqueness of RO-PUF is less efficient than its counterpart, arbiter PUFs. This paper proposes highly unique or random outputs of RO-PUF using a crossover technique among different inverters in the RO chains. The Challenge Response Pairs (CRPs) of the proposed design deliver heightened randomness that may apply to cryptography key generation. The design is implemented in the Proteus tool and tested in the NIST randomness test suit. A significant small statistical p-value for the proposed approach results in a robust randomized output. The results show that the randomness of the output frequency is extreme compared to other PUFs.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Different AGNR RTD
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: The graphene nanoribbon-based resonant-tunneling diodes (RTDs) have lately grabbed the interest of numerous scientists. In this paper, we have investigated the performance of double and triple-barrier hetero-structure armchair graphene nanoribbon (AGNR) RTD and made a comparison between them. The investigation shows that triple barrier hetero-structure (TBHS) RTD has superior characteristics in terms of peak-to-valley current ratio (PVR) and power dissipated at the valley current. In addition, we compared the performance of the double barrier hetero-structure (DBHS) with the electrostatically doped (ED) AGNR RTD. We discover that the hetero-structure RTD has a superior peak-to-valley current ratio and valley current power dissipation characteristics. Our article also examines the effect of a single vacancy defect in the barrier and well regions of a double barrier hetero-structure (DBHS) AGNR RTD. Introducing a single vacancy defect in the well region decreases the PVR and increases the power dissipated at the valley current. Introducing a single vacancy defect in the barrier area, on the other hand, enhances the PVR and lowers the power wasted by the valley current.

articleTitle: Methods for Detecting Epilepsy: A Comparative Analysis on Improved Deep Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Conditions affecting the brain, such as epilepsy, can be diagnosed with the help of electroencephalograms (EEGs). To analyze EEG signals, Deep Learning Algorithms have been proved very effective and efficient tools to detect epileptic seizures. In this work, we proposed a unique Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) architecture to differentiate epileptic people from the healthy counterpart. RNN is the improved version of previous ChronoNet and a ConvNet, and it consists of six convolution-max-pool blocks, followed by three standard convolution-average-pool blocks and one convolution-global_average-pool and a dense softmax classification layer. The deep Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) layers are piled on top of each other and tightly coupled in a feed-forward fashion in proposed ChronoNet, wherein each ID convolution layer uses multiple filters of progressively increasing lengths. The proposed ChronoNet architecture utilizes six ID convolution layer of different filter size while ConvNet Model implements six ID convolution layer of the same filter size. Using the same framework, Keras, the proposed improved ChronoNet and Deep CNN (ConvNet) architectures have been implemented using the data found at Temple University Hospital EEG Corpus and it was found that the improved ChronoNet outperforms the ConvNet yielding accuracies of around 97.20% and 88.14% respectively.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Broadband and Tunable Short-length Polarization Splitter on Photonic Crystal Fiber
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: We propose a straightforward dual-core photonic crystal fiber-based polarization splitter having extraordinary characteristics. Due to the nematic liquid crystal infilling, the mode birefringence increases significantly, enabling the splitter to attain a wide bandwidth of 356 nm, by keeping extinction ratio greater than 20 dB, and a short splitting length of 71.35 $\mu$m. The best performance is observed at 1550 nm of wavelength with a maximum extinction ratio of 83.3 dB. Additionally, the device could be thermally tuned to operate it within 1200 nm to 1650 nm of wavelength, thanks to the nematic liquid crystal infiltration. Hence, the device is a good match for current splitters due to its wide bandwidth, compact size, and tuning ability.

articleTitle: A bioinformatics approach to identify candidate biomarkers and common pathways between bipolar disorder and stroke
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Bipolar disorder (BD) is a severe psychiatric disease that is associated with a variety of physical disorders that substantially contribute to morbidity and mortality. People with BD now face a higher risk of stroke in recent years. The goal of this work is to identify therapeutic candidates and associated pathways with the help of a number of bioinformatics techniques. GSE23848 and GSE58294 microarray datasets are utilized for BD and stroke samples. Datasets are preprocessed and screened by making using R language, and then concordant differentially expressed genes (DEGs) are found. The DEGs’ regulatory structure is illustrated with a venn diagram. After that, protein-protein interactions (PPIs) are constructed based on the concordant DEGs and the most active genes are discovered using topological assessment. CBL, LY96, TLR5, TRAF6, and TLR4 are the leading 5 hub genes in the PPI network. The pathways of KEGG showed that the concordant DEGs are associated with the Toll-like receptor signaling pathway and Hepatitis B. Gene ontology (GO), TF and miRNA analysis and module analysis network is considered the future work of this research. Finally, the assortment of drug compounds have been suggested based on the concordant DEGs.

articleTitle: Cross-connected Multi Level Multi Input Inverter for Low Harmonics Operation
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Multilevel inverter performance is up scaled dramatically since it has the potential of reducing passive filters, increasing efficiency and power density. With more confining regulations regarding harmonic emission, more levels are required to allow output filter less operation. This paper proposes a multi input multilevel (thirteen level) inverter which comprises the promising features of low harmonics at its output voltage and current. This topology requires minimum number of switching devices for a given number of levels.

articleTitle: Hybrid QPSO assisted Incremental Conductance MPPT Algorithm under Extreme Partial Shading Conditions
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) technology has seen rapid growth over the last decade owing to its declining cost and minimal pollution. However, one major drawback of the PV systems is the non-linear characteristics of its output power under partial shading conditions (PSC). Varying weather parameters such as temperature and solar irradiance result in a multi-peak maximum power point tracking (MPPT) problem. To resolve this, many conventional and metaheuristic optimization MPPT algorithms have been proposed, some of which come with problems like slow tracking speed, increased oscillation, and no guarantee of convergence at the global maximum power point (GMPP). This paper presents a hybrid quantum particle swarm optimization assisted variable incremental conductance (QPSOVIC) algorithm which efficiently tracks maximum power (P<inf>max</inf>) under varying weather conditions. This metaheuristic algorithm overcomes the conventional tracking algorithm’s inability to track the GMPP and bypasses premature convergence of the traditional PSO algorithm. MATLAB/Simulink has been used for modeling and demonstration of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Analysis of Traction Power of Electric Three Wheelers in Bangladesh
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: The traction loads supplied by the electric three-wheeler (E3W) vehicles in different drive cycles in Bangladesh are determined and analyzed here. Four real-time drive cycles have been developed; two are from a city, one from a suburban region, and one from a village area. The traction power determination process has been presented considering the features of the E3Ws and velocity profile from drive cycles, along with additional information such as passenger number and distance covered. The traction power is compared with the motor rating to show the underload and the overload operation over the drive cycles. The prospect of regenerative braking of the E3W vehicles is explored, and the sensitivity of traction power demand against tire rolling resistance coefficient is examined under the four drive cycles developed.

articleTitle: Analysis of brain signal on visual noise affecting driver’s attention using deep learning
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: One of the main reasons for road accidents is driver’s brain activities during driving, some of which is heavily influenced by roadside visuals like posters, billboards and other objects around. Our objective is to prove that those posters, billboards, and roadside activities are some of the reasons for driver’s distraction that create high arousal on negative valence in certain part of driver’s brain and causes frequent road accidents. Our experiment shows that images of visually distasteful creates quite opposite reaction to that images of visually pleasing to human brain. Taking pictures from different locations of Dhaka city representing the actual roadside scenario that produces high stimulation in brain and can lead to human errors. In this research, brain data was collected using EEG device by displaying categorically positive, negative, and neutral pictures to the viewers. Collected brain data was analyzed using Deep Learning techniques. From the result, this research established strong correlations between different categories of images and the neural activities in the brain. The results are conclusive about perturbation on visually distracting elements along the roadside which may contribute to minor to major road accidents.

articleTitle: Segmented Linear Discriminant Analysis for Hyperspectral Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2022 12th International Conference on Electrical and Computer Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Remote sensing Hyperspectral Image (HSI) comprises significant information about the earth’s surface which is actually acquired by hundred of narrow and adjacent spectral bands. The intended performance of classification accuracy does not attain due to the volume of the original HSI dataset and the enormous quantity of spectral bands. As such, dimensionality reduction approaches using feature extraction and selection are typically adopted to enhance classification performance. The unsupervised Principal Component Analysis (PCA), as well as the supervised Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), are commonly used as linear feature extraction methods for feature subspace detection. However, due to considering the effects of global variation, both PCA and LDA fail to extract local characteristics of HSI. In this paper, we propose a segmented LDA-based (SLDA) feature extraction where we apply the LDA in a segmented way to extract better local characteristics as well as global characteristics from the HSI. Per-pixel classification using a Support Vector Machine (SVM) is applied to our proposed SLDA method, PCA, Segmented-PCA (SPCA), and LDA on the Indian Pines agricultural HSI dataset. The experimental results show that the overall classification performance of SLDA (90.60%) remarkably outperforms all the other investigated methods: PCA (85.55%), SPCA (86.96%), LDA (86.45%), and the complete original dataset without employing any feature reduction method (83.10%). The proposed SLDA also requires the least amount of space complexity in different implementation scenarios.
